mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport SV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A reconditioned or rebuilt Range Rover Sport SV engine typically costs between £10,000 and £18,000 for the supply-only unit, reflecting the ultra-premium nature and SV-specific fortifications of the 4.4L Twin-Turbo V8.
- Rebuilt units include upgraded cooling pathways and metal timing tensioners.
- Supply and fit packages are available through our ultra-premium specialist network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of hot-vee turbo or valve seal failure in a Range Rover Sport SV?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your Range Rover Sport SV engine and exhaust system.
- Look for blue smoke from the exhaust on cold startup or after idling, indicating oil leaking past hardened valve stem seals.
- Listen for a distinct rattling noise from the top of the engine on cold start, or check for unexplained coolant loss near the turbo housings.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an ultra-high-value Range Rover Sport SV?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, given the exceptional retained values of the SV flagship, replacing the engine is a highly sound financial decision.
- A typical 2023+ SV is valued between £100,000 and £140,000+, making a £12,000-£18,000 rebuild a small percentage of the vehicle's worth.
- A rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty adds reliability and protects your premium performance asset.

mainEntity.name: Can I use a standard P530 4.4L V8 engine in my Range Rover Sport SV?

acceptedAnswer.text:
While the hardware architecture is similar, a direct swap is not recommended without extensive modification.
- The SV engine features specific internal fortifications, upgraded cooling pathways, and bespoke SV Department ECU mapping to handle 635hp safely.
- We strongly recommend sourcing an SV-specific replacement or a heavily fortified rebuild to ensure guaranteed compatibility, reliability, and warranty coverage.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Sport SV engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A straightforward supply and fit replacement for a Range Rover Sport SV typically takes 5 to 8 days at an ultra-premium specialist workshop.
- This allows time for the engine to be delivered, mounted, and thoroughly calibrated using SV-specific diagnostic tools.
- Complex cases requiring additional cooling system or exhaust recalibrations may take slightly longer.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Sport SV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Sport SV features a heavily fortified 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8 based on the BMW N63 architecture, tuned by the SV Department to deliver 635hp. While immensely powerful, the hot-vee turbocharger layout generates extreme thermal stress, requiring meticulous maintenance. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: Valve Stem Seal Wear & Turbo Cooling Leaks
problems.h4: Valve Stem Seal Wear & Turbo Cooling Leaks - Why the Range Rover Sport SV 4.4L Twin-Turbo V8 Requires Attention
problems.affectedModels: Range Rover Sport SV (4.4L Twin-Turbo V8, 2023-present)
problems.rootCause: The hot-vee design places turbochargers inside the cylinder bank V, subjecting valve stem seals and turbo coolant lines to extreme thermal cycling. Seals harden and leak oil into the exhaust (causing blue smoke), while coolant lines degrade and leak under high boost pressures.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip top end to replace valve stem seals, upgrade turbo coolant lines with revised OEM parts, and perform smoke testing.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early before oil fouls the catalytic converters or turbo cores.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, SV-fortified internal components, upgraded cooling pathways, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if severe oil burning has damaged catalytic converters or if bottom-end bearing wear is present.

problems.recommendation: If your SV exhibits early signs of valve seal wear or timing chain rattle, invest in preventative specialist repairs immediately to protect the catalytic converters and turbos. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic timing failure or severe bottom-end knock from oil starvation, a full reconditioned replacement using SV-fortified components is the only safe path to protect your investment.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Stretch - Why the Range Rover Sport SV 4.4L Twin-Turbo V8 Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Range Rover Sport SV (4.4L Twin-Turbo V8, 2023-present)
problems.rootCause: The immense torque generated by the 635hp SV calibration places extreme stress on the timing chain guides and tensioners. Premature stretch causes a distinct cold-start rattle and risks chain skip, leading to catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip front covers, replace timing chains, guides, and upgraded metal tensioners.
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended preventative maintenance if cold-start rattle is detected before engine damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain failure has already caused internal valvetrain or piston damage.
